before.text: ext/goal/src/background_wait.rs: gate goal continuation only, check-in tickets, warning text, invalidation. Detailed AC before spawn.

after.text: Goal-owned background waiting policy, inactive by default until activation story F (final plan section 6; stage 2d, leaf 2 of STORY p4a-goal-background-wait; verdict rev3 note 5: the admission contributor is new code). Intra-story order: runs after sibling TASK-260929-36bvsc (E1) is accepted and checkpointed. New ext/goal/src/background_wait.rs. Gate ONLY automatic goal continuation, never user or follow-up admission, and never inter-agent or trigger mail (trigger-mail priority stays authoritative; global idle suppression is forbidden because it would starve queue work). At goal continuation (ext/goal/src/runtime.rs continuation path) read the E1 snapshot. When known pending work exists, do not continue: wait for events. Recheck pending state and revision in a NEW goal automatic-admission contributor in core/src/session/turn_input.rs (re-locate the plan's 410-447 citation). Either serialize the last check with reservation/receipt transitions, or reject when the revision changed. Never hold the goal semaphore during a delay. Fallback check-in timers of 30, 60 and 120 minutes, at most three per human input. A timer ticket permits exactly one check-in that bypasses this work gate only. It bypasses no status, Plan, shutdown, capacity, input or newer-turn checks. Reassess after each check-in. After the third check-in, emit exactly once the warning 'Automatic check-ins stopped; waiting for subscribed work or your next message.' The goal remains active and event-wakeable, never marked paused, blocked or complete. Human input renews the allowance. A completion pre-empts timers without counting as human input. Invalidate tickets on steering, turn start, goal mutation, clear, stop and release; resume discards stale waits. Releasing a mis-armed subscription allows paced continuation without a kill. A failed snapshot read is not 'no pending work'. Use the safe behavior (no automatic continuation past the gate) and state it. Use deterministic or fake time, never real sleeps.

AC1 Queue fairness: with pending exec work, user and follow-up input and queued or trigger mail are still admitted immediately. Only goal continuation is gated. AC2 Read failure is never treated as empty: goal continuation does not proceed past the gate on a failed read (narrowing mutant: treat error as empty). AC3 Inactive and budget-limited goal status, and an unopted or server-only process, do not engage the gate. AC4 Check-ins fire at 30, 60 and 120 minutes (fake time), at most three per human input. Each ticket bypasses only the work gate, exactly once (a mutant allowing repeated bypass must fail). AC5 After the third check-in the exact warning text is emitted once. The goal status stays active and wakeable. AC6 A completion that arrives after the cap wakes the goal, and is not counted as human input. AC7 Gate-to-start race: a receipt transition between the continuation check and turn start is caught by the admission contributor's revision recheck (latch test; mutant skips the recheck). AC8 Release of a mis-armed subscription lets paced continuation proceed without killing the process. AC9 Tickets are invalidated on steering, turn start, goal mutation, clear, stop and release, and resume discards stale waits. AC10 The goal semaphore is not held across a delay (assertion or test).

Production `Session::new` shares one `pending_work_revision` counter between the receipt store and the input queue, so E1 transitions bump the same revision the admission contributor rechecks.
